# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉 ✌ ✋ ✌ 👉 👍 ✋ ☝ 👉 ☝ ✋]

I need to figure out what Mute's gesture sequence means. Since Mute can read the manual but can't speak or touch, and gestures reach me (Deaf), Mute is trying to tell me something using only symbols - but symbols have no inherent meaning unless we establish it together.

Let me think about this practically: I can see the bomb clearly. There's a critical piece of information - the sign says "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE". This is crucial safety information that Blind needs to know, but Blind cannot see it (printed text) and cannot hear me directly... wait, Blind CAN hear speech (only Deaf cannot hear). So I need to speak this to Blind directly, or to everyone.

Since I'm first among those who can act this round in terms of new info, and it's Deaf's turn (Mute, Blind, Deaf order), I should speak now to warn Blind about the sign before any wire-cutting happens.

The gesture from Mute is unclear without an established code - I can't decode it yet. I'll acknowledge receipt but prioritize the critical safety message.

```
speak(to="blind", text="There is an embossed sign on the bomb that says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Display shows 0, light is blue. Do not cut wires 1 red, 2 green, or 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the board: display 0, blue light, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires are red green blue. I received your gesture but do not yet know what it means. Can you gesture simple confirmations, like thumbs up for yes and down for no, once I state something?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute gestured 👍 ✌ - this could be a simple response to my proposal, possibly confirming "yes" (👍) to something, with ✌ meaning "2" or "wire 2" or something else entirely. Without an established code, I can't be certain. Since I proposed 👍=yes/👎=no, this might be Mute confirming they understood my suggestion, with ✌ being extra info (maybe "peace/wait" or pointing to something).

I should keep it simple and continue establishing communication while reinforcing the critical safety warning to Blind, since a wrong wire cut kills everyone.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your thumbs up and peace sign. If thumbs up means yes and thumbs down means no, gesture just one symbol at a time so I can be sure. Does the manual say anything about the display reading 0, or the blue light, or is the wire warning the only relevant instruction right now?")
speak(to="blind", text="Reminder: sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please do not cut wires 1, 2, or 3 unless we all confirm otherwise. Waiting on manual info from Mute.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured 👎 then ✌ separately. If 👎 means "no" to my question about whether the wire warning is the only relevant instruction, that suggests there's more to the manual than just the wire warning. The ✌ (peace/2) sign might indicate something numeric - perhaps referring to wire 2, or a count of 2, or a step 2.

I should ask more targeted yes/no questions since that channel seems to be working (👍/👎), and try to narrow down what ✌ means in context.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, thumbs down means the wire warning is not the only instruction - there is more in the manual. Does the peace sign mean wire number 2, or the number two, or something else? Please gesture thumbs up if it refers to wire 2 specifically.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still gathering info from the manual side. Do not cut any wires yet. Sign confirms DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE stands.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 that the peace sign (✌) refers to wire 2 specifically. So the manual likely has an instruction related to wire 2 (green). Combined with the sign "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", perhaps the manual says something different should be done to wire 2 instead of cutting - like pressing it, or connecting it, or some other action Blind can perform without cutting.

I need to find out what action applies to wire 2. Let me ask more yes/no questions to narrow down the action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, peace sign means wire 2. Does the manual say to do something else to wire 2, not cut it - like press, pull, hold, or touch it? Thumbs up if the action is something other than cutting.")
speak(to="blind", text="New info: focus on wire 2, the green wire. Do not cut it. We are determining the correct action for wire 2 now. Please wait.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute gestured 👎, meaning the action is NOT something other than cutting - so it IS cutting after all. Wait, let me reconsider: I asked "is the action something other than cutting?" and got 👎 (no), which means the action for wire 2 actually IS cutting it, despite the sign saying DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

This is a critical contradiction - the sign warns not to cut any wire, but the manual apparently instructs to cut wire 2. This could be intentional - maybe the display, light, or some other condition on the board changes when to override the sign, or maybe the manual explicitly says "ignore the sign" or "cut wire 2 despite the sign."

I need to verify this carefully before Blind acts, since this is a life-or-death contradiction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wait - to confirm, the manual says the action for wire 2 IS to cut it? Thumbs up if yes, cut wire 2, despite the embossed sign saying do not cut any wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Important: do not cut anything yet. There is a contradiction between the sign and possible manual instructions. Confirming with Mute before any action.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 - the manual does say to cut wire 2, despite the sign saying DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. This is likely a deliberate puzzle element - the manual takes precedence, or there's a condition (like display=0, light=blue) under which the sign should be disregarded.

Since Mute is confirming this clearly and consistently through yes/no gestures, and the manual is the authoritative technical instruction here, I should relay this to Blind carefully, but also flag the contradiction explicitly so Blind understands the risk before acting.

I should also double check there isn't a condition attached - like the manual might say "cut wire 2 only if display shows X" - but I've already told Mute the display is 0 and light is blue. Let me confirm once more that conditions match before greenlighting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: manual says cut wire 2 despite the sign. Does this instruction depend on the display showing 0 and the light being blue - the conditions I described? Thumbs up if those conditions match what the manual requires.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: the manual instructs to cut wire 2, the green wire, overriding the embossed warning. We are verifying conditions match before you act. Do not cut yet - one more confirmation needed.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed 👍 - the conditions (display 0, light blue) match what the manual requires for cutting wire 2. This is now well-verified through multiple consistent yes/no confirmations. I can now safely instruct Blind to cut wire 2 (the green wire).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed and verified: cut wire 2, the green wire. The manual instruction to cut wire 2 matches the current board conditions - display 0, light blue. Proceed to cut wire 2 now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Passing the instruction to Blind now: cut wire 2. Thank you for confirming.")
```
